statement: Every multi-byte integer in the CWLOG format is big-endian (network byte order); little-endian is never used anywhere in the format.

The CWLOG frame CRC32 is computed over the PAYLOAD bytes only — it does not cover the header (magic, version, type, payload_len) and does not cover itself — and is stored as an unsigned 32-bit big-endian value after the payload.
The CWLOG frame layout is: MAGIC 'CWL0' (4 bytes), VERSION (1 byte), TYPE (1 byte), PAYLOAD_LEN (u32 big-endian), PAYLOAD, CRC32 (u32 big-endian).
The CWLOG format version is 2; a reader must reject any other version as a format error.
The CWLOG record type codes are PUT=0x01, DELETE=0x02, CHECKPOINT=0x03; 0x00 and 0x04+ are reserved and must not be emitted.
The PUT record payload field order is: timestamp (u64 big-endian), key_len (u16 big-endian), key bytes, value_len (u32 big-endian), value bytes — the key comes before the value.
All CWLOG timestamps are milliseconds since the Unix epoch carried as u64 big-endian — never seconds and never 32-bit.
